claim: The inner detector is immersed in a 2 T solenoidal field.
Tracking: required resolution sigma_pT/pT = 0.05% pT (+) 1%, eta coverage +-2.5 (pT in GeV).
EM calorimetry: required resolution sigma_E/E = 10%/sqrt(E) (+) 0.7% (E in GeV).
Hadronic calorimetry (jets), barrel and end-cap: required resolution sigma_E/E = 50%/sqrt(E) (+) 3%.
Muon spectrometer: required resolution sigma_pT/pT = 10% at pT = 1 TeV.
The pixel intrinsic accuracies in the barrel are 10 um (R-phi) and 115 um (z).
The SCT intrinsic accuracies per module in the barrel are 17 um (R-phi) and 580 um (z).
The TRT provides typically 36 hits per track and has an intrinsic accuracy of 130 um per straw (R-phi only).
The pixel detector has approximately 80.4 million readout channels.
The dimensions of the detector are 25 m in height and 44 m in length; the overall weight is approximately 7000 tonnes.
The Level-1 trigger reduces the data rate to approximately 75 kHz (limited by the readout bandwidth, upgradeable to 100 kHz).
At the heart of CMS sits a 13-m-long, 6-m-inner-diameter, 4-T superconducting solenoid providing a large bending power (12 Tm).

claim: LHCb is a single-arm forward spectrometer covering the pseudorapidity range 2 < eta < 5.
The dipole magnet, unchanged with respect to Run 1-2, provides a vertical magnetic field with a bending power of about 4 Tm.
LHCb was originally designed to take data at a maximum instantaneous luminosity of 2 x 10^32 cm^-2 s^-1.
LHCb was operated for most of Run 1 and Run 2 at about 4 x 10^32 cm^-2 s^-1.
The upgrade is designed to run at a nominal instantaneous luminosity of 2 x 10^33 cm^-2 s^-1 and to collect events at the LHC crossing rate of 40 MHz.
Inner radius of the active silicon detector of the VELO: 8.2 mm (2009-2018).
Inner radius of the active silicon detector of the VELO: 5.1 mm (2022).
VELO pitch: 37-97 um r-phi strips (2009-2018); 55 um square pixels (2022).
VELO total number of channels: 172 thousand (2009-2018); 41 million (2022).
LHCb collected a total of 9 fb^-1 of proton-proton data during Run 1 and Run 2.

claim: The SK detector is a cylindrical tank (39.3 m diameter and 41.4 m height) filled with 50 kilotons of ultra-pure water.
The detector is located 1000 m underground (2,700 m water equivalent) in the Kamioka mine.
SK-I (1996 Apr. - 2001 Jul.) had 11146 inner-detector PMTs (40% photo-coverage).
SK-II (2002 Oct. - 2005 Oct.) had 5182 inner-detector PMTs (19% photo-coverage).
SK-III (2006 Jul. - 2008 Sep.) and SK-IV (from 2008 Sep.) had 11129 inner-detector PMTs (40% photo-coverage).
The outer detector has 1885 PMTs.
The electronics were upgraded in September 2008; SK-IV uses the QBEE front-end electronics.
The timing resolution was 2.1 ns at the one-photoelectron charge level and 0.5 ns at the 100-photoelectron charge level.
